title: What Are the Baltic Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Publish method: update in place, change slug and path to /expert-advice/baltic-wedding-traditions, confirm the old URL returns a 301. Check for separate Lithuanian, Latvian or Estonian pages (301 or cross-link). Protect its rankings.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch (retry with a render wait if no body), confirms it is about the Baltics and records its 10 headings; SEO pulls its ranked keywords (US and AU), checks duplicate Lithuanian/Latvian/Estonian pages, and the outline keeps covering every query with real volume. Keep sourceable traditions; never reuse wording; drop errors.

THREE COUNTRIES: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language, customs and law. Say so once, then tie every custom to the country its source names. Nothing pan-Baltic unless a source says so.
Culture, not politics: no commentary on regional history or relations with neighbours.

Likely customs (brief finalises): Latvian mičošana / Lithuanian equivalent (veil or wreath replaced by a married woman's headdress); Estonian bonnet ceremony (tanu panek); bridal 'kidnapping' as light play; bridges and padlocks if sourced; bread and salt welcome; thresholds and obstacles on the way; the wreath; the dowry chest (kraičio skrynia, pūrs); songs and dances. Terms with diacritics as sources give them.

UNESCO only where its own text links an element to weddings: Baltic Song and Dance Celebrations (2008); Lithuanian sutartinės (2010); Seto leelo (2009); Kihnu cultural space (2008); Suiti cultural space (2009). Confirm each page live and title.

Destination angle: Smartraveller checked live for all three countries, including higher-level areas. Legal from official sources only: the Australian embassy or consulate covering each country (found live); Smartraveller CNI and 'Getting married overseas' (recognition); civil registry steps only if an official page can be read; otherwise 'check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'. Baltic-Australian weddings at home, as relevant.

Sources: UNESCO, national museums, culture ministries, official tourism sites (visitestonia.com, latvia.travel, lithuania.travel), encyclopaedias, academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' with no meanings as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker. One honest framing line per section.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (wreath, bread) labelled illustrative pending approval; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: Latvia and Lithuania; B: Estonia, UNESCO and legal), 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
